thread.title: More Apple iPhone Buyers Seeking Higher-End Models, Survey Shows | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: More Apple iPhone Buyers Seeking Higher-End Models, Survey Shows | Investor's Business Daily
text:
A larger-than-expected percentage of likely Apple ( AAPL ) iPhone buyers is looking to get higher-end models this product cycle, a Wall Street firm said Monday.
X That bodes well for iPhone average selling prices and profit margins, Piper Jaffray said, based on its survey of over 700 U.S. iPhone owners.
The survey showed 39% would get the iPhone XS or XS Max if they were to upgrade this year. Those respondents were nearly evenly split between the 5.8-inch iPhone XS and 6.5-inch iPhone XS Max. Piper previously estimated that only 35% of upgrades would come from the OLED-screen XS models.
The remaining 61% of prospective iPhone buyers plan to get either the upcoming iPhone XR or the now lower-priced iPhone 7 and 8 models, Piper said.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Based on the survey results, Piper analyst Michael Olson raised his estimate for the iPhone average selling price. He sees it at $770 for fiscal 2019, up from his prior estimate of $758. Apple's fiscal 2019 started Sunday. Wall Street's current consensus for iPhone average selling price this fiscal year is $768, Olson said.
Interest In iPhone XR Seen Growing The iPhone's average selling price could reach $780 in fiscal 2019. That's if the midrange iPhone XR sells better than expected, he said. Olson said his current expectation is for the iPhone XR to get 30% of iPhone sales this cycle. The 6.1-inch LCD-screen iPhone XR goes on sale Oct. 26 after a week of preorders.
"Considering Apple has not yet started marketing for iPhone XR, we expect interest for that device to grow in the coming weeks," Olson said in a note to clients.
Olson maintained his overweight rating on Apple stock with a price target of 250.
Apple shares rose 0.7% to 227.26 on the stock market today . It is just below its all-time high of 229.67, reached on Sept. 5.
